ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Keep the current matrix and dashboard structure, but make skill progression internally consistent: visually distinguish learned, currently unlockable, and locked nodes and ensure connecting lines agree with those states. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Make the selected node the unmistakable bridge between tree and detail: strengthen its outgoing visual relationship to the right-hand ability panel while reducing the panel's independent glow. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Define explicit node tokens for locked, available, selected, and keystone states using consistent diameters, two ring widths, and controlled glow levels; terminate every connector exactly beneath the outer ring and normalize line weight and color by state. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Give each skill branch a content-specific visual motif and silhouette, introduce one memorable capstone node and semantically varied node scales, and extend the celestial discipline theme into bespoke icons and restrained constellation textures rather than adding arbitrary colors. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Keep the current matrix and dashboard structure, but make skill progression internally consistent: visually distinguish learned, currently unlockable, and locked nodes and ensure connecting lines agree with those states.—while using the clarity action—Make the selected node the unmistakable bridge between tree and detail: strengthen its outgoing visual relationship to the right-hand ability panel while reducing the panel's independent glow.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Define explicit node tokens for locked, available, selected, and keystone states using consistent diameters, two ring widths, and controlled glow levels; terminate every connector exactly beneath the outer ring and normalize line weight and color by state.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Give each skill branch a content-specific visual motif and silhouette, introduce one memorable capstone node and semantically varied node scales, and extend the celestial discipline theme into bespoke icons and restrained constellation textures rather than adding arbitrary colors.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
